### FINDING 1 — FATAL — location: title
CLAIM AS WRITTEN: "The particular-point topology is $T_0$ and not $T_1$, it is not regular once the set has at least two points, and it is not normal once the set has at least three"

WHY IT FAILS: The title asserts "not $T_1$" as an unconditional property of "the particular-point topology," parallel to the unconditioned "$T_0$" clause right before it, and distinct from the "not regular" and "not normal" clauses which the same sentence *does* explicitly condition on set size ("once the set has at least two points" / "once the set has at least three"). But the body's own claim 2 and its proof (step 1.3) prove "not $T_1$" only "If $X$ has at least two points." When $|X|=1$, i.e. $X=\{p\}$, the construction is still a legitimate instance (nothing in the Given data or in `def-standard-topologies` item 5 requires $|X|\ge2$): $\mathcal{T}_p=\{\varnothing,\{p\}\}$, the discrete topology on a singleton. `def-t0-and-t1-spaces` states directly: "a space with at most one point satisfies both conditions \[$T_0$ and $T_1$\] vacuously." So at $|X|=1$ the space *is* $T_1$, and the title's blanket "not $T_1$" is false in that case — while the title correctly hedges the very next two clauses with exactly this kind of size qualifier. This is precisely the "title asserts more than the proof gives" defect: the Statement/body is fully correct and properly hedges every conditional claim, but the title drops the hedge for one of them.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT: Add the same qualifier used for "not regular" to the "not $T_1$" clause, e.g. "...is $T_0$, is not $T_1$ once the set has at least two points, is not regular once the set has at least two points, and is not normal once the set has at least three."

### ASSESSMENT
The mathematical content — Statement clauses 1–4, the Facts block citations ([A1], [L1], [L2] against `def-standard-topologies`, `def-t0-and-t1-spaces`, `thm-t1-iff-singletons-are-closed`, `def-hausdorff-space`, `def-regular-and-t3-spaces`, `def-normal-and-t4-spaces`), and every proof step (1.1–4.1) — is correct, and the repair (deleting the now-unused `[L3]` fact after removing the closure-based approach, adding `provenance`, and the Sierpiński-space reference URL) introduces no new false claim; the fetched Sierpiński-space source confirms exactly the properties the item's Remarks and cited companion example (`ex-sierpinski-space-is-t0-normal-and-not-regular`) assert. `def-interior-closure-boundary-top` is now an orphaned entry in `deps:` (unused anywhere in the current body) but is not cited by the Facts block or Remarks, so it's a stale-dependency housekeeping issue, not a mathematical defect. The one fatal issue is the title's unconditioned "not $T_1$," which contradicts the body's own correctly-hedged claim 2 in the genuine edge case $|X|=1$.
